claims.claim: Ruby only issues the calls to libvips; Ruby overhead per image is likely a few milliseconds
claims.why: The measurements cover Rails HTTP request handling. They do not cover the per-job overhead of a Sidekiq worker issuing libvips calls, so the per-image Ruby cost can't be checked.

claims.claim: Rewriting in Go or Rust would speed up the thin layer around libvips, not the 150–400 ms of image work; the gains are small because the work is in libvips and the model
claims.about: Go/Rust vs Ruby for the image-processing worker
claims.why: The CPU test shows Rust and Go far ahead of Ruby on pure-language fib(20) (about 27–29k and 15–18k req/s vs 3,068), but nothing measures a workload where the time goes to C libraries or ML inference, so the claim can't be checked either way.

claims.claim: A faster runtime such as ONNX Runtime is a lever for speeding up the tagging model
claims.why: None of the benchmarks include ML inference runtimes.
